component.name: milo-browse
component.title: OPC UA Browser
component.description: Browse the nodes of an OPC UA server and the references between them.
component.label: iot

clientId.description: An ID that is part of the key of the shared connections: endpoints with the same endpoint URI, requestedPublishingInterval and clientId use the same connection to the server. Set a different value to give an endpoint a connection of its own.

configuration.description: The client configuration that holds the default options of the endpoints of this component. Each endpoint uses a copy of it, with the options that are set on the endpoint.

discoveryEndpointSuffix.description: A suffix that the client appends to the endpoint URI to get the URI of the discovery endpoint, for example /discovery. Not used when discoveryEndpointUri is set.

discoveryEndpointUri.description: The URI of the discovery endpoint that the client gets the endpoint descriptions of the server from, instead of the endpoint URI. It takes precedence over discoveryEndpointSuffix.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

allowedSecurityPolicies.label: client
allowedSecurityPolicies.description: A comma-separated list of the security policies that the client may use, as URIs or as names of org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.security.SecurityPolicy, for example Basic256Sha256. Of the endpoints of the server with an allowed policy, the client uses the one with the highest security level. If not set, every policy is allowed, None included.

applicationName.label: client
applicationName.defaultValue: Apache Camel adapter for Eclipse Milo
applicationName.description: The application name of the client, which it sends to the server in its application description.

applicationUri.label: client
applicationUri.description: The application URI of the client, which it sends to the server in its application description. With a client certificate, it should match the application URI in that certificate.

channelLifetime.label: client
channelLifetime.description: The requested lifetime in milliseconds of the security token of the secure channel, after which the client renews it. If not set, the default of Eclipse Milo is used.

keyAlias.label: client
keyAlias.description: The alias of the private key and its certificate in the key store. It can be omitted when the key store holds a single entry.

keyPassword.label: client
keyPassword.description: The password of the private key of keyAlias in the key store.

keyStorePassword.label: client
keyStorePassword.description: The password of the key store of keyStoreUrl.

keyStoreType.label: client
keyStoreType.description: The type of the key store of keyStoreUrl, as a java.security.KeyStore type. The default is PKCS12.

keyStoreUrl.label: client
keyStoreUrl.description: The URL of the key store with the certificate and the private key of the client, for example file:/etc/opcua/client.p12. A security policy other than None needs it.

maxPendingPublishRequests.label: client
maxPendingPublishRequests.description: The maximum number of publish requests that the client keeps pending at the server for its subscription. If not set, the default of Eclipse Milo is used.

maxResponseMessageSize.label: client
maxResponseMessageSize.description: The maximum size in bytes of a response message that the client accepts from the server. If not set, the default of Eclipse Milo is used.

miloClientConnectionManager.label: client
miloClientConnectionManager.description: To use a custom org.apache.camel.component.milo.client.MiloClientConnectionManager that creates and releases the connections to the OPC UA servers. The default one shares a connection between the endpoints with the same endpoint URI, clientId, requestedPublishingInterval and validation of the server certificate, and closes it when the last endpoint releases it.

overrideHost.label: client
overrideHost.description: Whether to replace the host of the endpoint URL that the server reports with the host of the endpoint URI. Use it when the server reports a host name that the client cannot reach.

overridePort.label: client
overridePort.description: Whether to replace the port of the endpoint URL that the server reports with the port of the endpoint URI. Use it when the server reports a port that the client cannot reach.

productUri.label: client
productUri.description: The product URI of the client, which it sends to the server in its application description.

reconnectTimeout.label: client
reconnectTimeout.description: The delay in milliseconds before the client tries again to connect to the server after an attempt failed, and between two attempts to create the monitored items that the server refused. Neither attempt is made while the OPC UA client recovers a lost session on its own.

requestedPublishingInterval.label: client
requestedPublishingInterval.description: The publishing interval in milliseconds that the client requests for the subscription of its connection, which carries the values of the monitored nodes. Endpoints with different values use different connections.

requestTimeout.label: client
requestTimeout.description: The timeout in milliseconds of a request to the server. If not set, the default of Eclipse Milo is used.

sessionName.label: client
sessionName.description: The name of the session that the client creates on the server. If not set, Eclipse Milo generates one.

sessionTimeout.label: client
sessionTimeout.description: The requested timeout in milliseconds of the session, after which the server closes a session without activity. If not set, the default of Eclipse Milo is used.

certificateValidator.label: security
certificateValidator.description: A custom validator for the certificate of the OPC UA server. When set, it is used instead of the trust list configured with trustListDirectory. Endpoints share a connection only when they use the same validator instance.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for authentication. Use this instead of embedding credentials in the endpoint URI when the password contains special characters (such as ?, /, , &).

trustAllCertificates.label: security
trustAllCertificates.description: Whether to accept any certificate presented by the OPC UA server. This is insecure: the connection is encrypted, but the client does not authenticate the server it talks to. It only applies when neither certificateValidator nor trustListDirectory is configured.

trustListDirectory.label: security
trustListDirectory.description: The directory holding the trust list used to validate the certificate of the OPC UA server, in the layout used by Eclipse Milo: trusted certificates in trusted/certs, CRLs of trusted certificates in trusted/crl, certificates of issuing CAs in issuer/certs and their CRLs in issuer/crl. The directories are created if they do not exist. Besides the chain of trust, the validity period, the revocation by a CRL of the trust list and the application URI of the server certificate are checked. A certificate issued by a CA is refused when the trust list holds no CRL of that CA; an empty CRL is enough. A server certificate that does not chain up to a trusted certificate is written to rejected/certs, from where it can be moved to trusted/certs once it has been checked.

username.label: security
username.description: The username for authentication. Use this instead of embedding credentials in the endpoint URI when the username contains special characters (such as ?, /, , &).

CamelMiloNodeIds.label: producer
CamelMiloNodeIds.description: A List of node IDs. The milo-client producer reads the values of these nodes instead of writing the body. The milo-browse producer browses from these nodes instead of the node option, and sets the header to the List of the node IDs that it found.

producerIn.description: The body is not read: the nodes to browse are the node IDs of the CamelMiloNodeIds header, or else the node option

producerOut.description: A Map of the browsed ExpandedNodeId to its Milo BrowseResult; the node IDs found are also in the CamelMiloNodeIds header, as a List of Strings for the milo-client producer

endpointUri.description: The endpoint URL of the OPC UA server, for example opc.tcp://localhost:4840/path. It can hold a user name and password in its user info part. The username and password options take precedence over them.

clientId.description: An ID that is part of the key of the shared connections: endpoints with the same endpoint URI, requestedPublishingInterval and clientId use the same connection to the server. Set a different value to give an endpoint a connection of its own.

depth.description: The number of levels that a recursive browse goes down, where the nodes to browse from are level 1. Only used when recursive is true. Default value notice: Maximum depth for browsing recursively (only if recursive = true)

direction.description: The direction of the references to follow: Forward, Inverse or Both. Default value notice: The direction to browse; see org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.enumerated.BrowseDirection

discoveryEndpointSuffix.description: A suffix that the client appends to the endpoint URI to get the URI of the discovery endpoint, for example /discovery. Not used when discoveryEndpointUri is set.

discoveryEndpointUri.description: The URI of the discovery endpoint that the client gets the endpoint descriptions of the server from, instead of the endpoint URI. It takes precedence over discoveryEndpointSuffix.

filter.description: A regular expression that the node ID of a found node, in its parseable form such as ns=2;s=item, must match to be in the result and to be browsed further. If not set, all nodes are kept. Default value notice: Regular filter expression matching node ids

includeSubTypes.description: Whether to follow the references of all subtypes of the References reference type. If false, only references of the abstract References type itself are returned, which are usually none. A recursive browse always includes the subtypes.

maxNodeIdsPerRequest.description: The maximum number of nodes that one Browse request asks for, when a recursive browse goes down to the next level. Default value notice: Maximum number of node ids requested per browse call (applies to browsing sub-types only; only if recursive = true)

node.description: The node ID of the node to browse from, for example ns=2;s=folder. The CamelMiloNodeIds header replaces this option. The default is the Root folder, i=84. Default value notice: Root folder as per OPC-UA spec

nodeClasses.description: A comma-separated list of the node classes of the nodes to return, as names of org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.enumerated.NodeClass: Object, Variable, Method, ObjectType, VariableType, ReferenceType, DataType and View. Default value notice: Comma-separated node class list; see org.eclipse.milo.opcua.stack.core.types.enumerated.NodeClass

recursive.description: Whether to browse the nodes that are found again, down to the level of the depth option. A recursive browse always includes the subtypes of the reference type, whatever includeSubTypes says. Default value notice: Whether to recursively browse sub-types: true|false
